rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed — only transformed. When only conservative forces act, mechanical energy (K + U) is conserved. Non-conservative forces (friction) convert mechanical energy to heat, but total energy is always conserved. The work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) is the key tool for solving problems.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mechanical energy conservation: K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f (only conservative forces)
Work-energy theorem: W_net = ΔK = ½mv_f² − ½mv_i²
Work by non-conservative forces: W_nc = ΔE_mech = (K_f + U_f) − (K_i + U_i)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Energy is NOT created or destroyed — it only transforms. When a pendulum stops swinging due to friction, the energy doesn't 'disappear'; it becomes thermal energy in the air and the pivot. The FIRST law of thermodynamics says energy is conserved in all processes.  ·  Conservation of mechanical energy (K + U = constant) ONLY holds when ALL forces are conservative. If there is ANY friction, air resistance, or non-conservative force, mechanical energy is NOT conserved. You must include W_nc or track thermal energy.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Mechanical energy conservation requires ALL forces to be conservative — one friction force breaks it.  ·  The reference level for gravitational PE is arbitrary — only differences matter.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Pendulum: A 2 kg bob is released from 0.5 m above the lowest point. Speed at bottom: mgh = ½mv² → v = √(2×9.8×0.5) = 3.13 m/s.  ·  Spring-mass: A 0.5 kg mass on a spring (k = 200 N/m) compressed 0.1 m. Max speed: ½kA² = ½mv² → v = √(200×0.01/0.5) = 2 m/s.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Potential energy is NOT absolute — it is defined relative to an arbitrary zero point. A ball on a table has U = mgh relative to the floor, but U = mg(h+H) relative to the basement. Only PE differences matter physically.  ·  In a collision, momentum is ALWAYS conserved (if no external forces). Kinetic energy is ONLY conserved in perfectly ELASTIC collisions. Many students think KE is always conserved in collisions — it is NOT. Real collisions are usually somewhat inelastic.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Solve 5 free-fall problems using mgh = ½mv².  ·  Solve 5 pendulum problems finding speed at the lowest point.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Smooth surface shortcut: mgh = ½mv² — mass cancels, so v = √(2gh) independent of mass.  ·  Spring shortcut: ½kA² = ½mv² — max speed v = A√(k/m).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: A 0.2 kg ball is dropped from 15 m. Find its speed just before hitting the ground.  ·  A 1.5 kg mass on a spring (k = 300 N/m) is stretched 0.2 m and released. Find the maximum speed.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Mechanical energy conservation (K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f) is the most common problem type.  ·  Work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) is more general — use it when friction is present.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed — only transformed from one form to another.  ·  Mechanical energy (K + U) is conserved when only conservative forces do work.  ·  The work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) holds for all forces, conservative or not.  ·  Non-conservative forces convert mechanical energy into thermal energy.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mechanical energy (K + U) is conserved ONLY when all forces are conservative.  ·  Friction and air resistance are non-conservative — they convert mechanical energy to heat.  ·  The work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) holds for ALL forces, conservative or not.  ·  Total energy (including thermal) is always conserved — this is the first law of thermodynamics.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The law of conservation of energy is the first law of thermodynamics and applies to ALL physical processes — mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics, general relativity. It is the most fundamental and universal law in physics.  ·  Emmy Noether proved (1918) that conservation of energy is a consequence of time translation symmetry: the laws of physics are the same at all times. This is Noether's theorem — every continuous symmetry implies a conserved quantity.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: A 600 kg roller coaster car starts at 25 m height. Find its speed at the bottom and at 10 m height.  ·  A 0.5 kg pendulum bob is pulled to 30° from vertical (length 1.2 m). Find its speed at the lowest point.  ·  A 2 kg block slides down a rough 40° slope (μ_k = 0.2) of length 8 m. Find the speed at the bottom.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Pendulum and spring problems are standard — know the energy oscillation formulas.  ·  Roller coaster and free-fall problems use mgh = ½mv² (smooth surface).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Roller coaster: A 500 kg car starts at 20 m height. Speed at bottom: v = √(2×9.8×20) = 19.8 m/s.  ·  Free fall: A 1 kg stone dropped from 45 m. Speed at ground: v = √(2×9.8×45) = 29.7 m/s.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A 2 kg ball is dropped from 20 m. Its speed just before hitting the ground is: (g = 10 m/s²) → B  ·  A spring (k = 400 N/m) is compressed 0.1 m. A 0.5 kg mass is placed against it. The maximum speed is: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Law of conservation of energy:** Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another or transferred between systems. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time.  ·  **Mechanical energy conservation:** When only conservative forces (gravity, spring force, electrostatic force) act on a system, mechanical energy E = K + U is conserved: ΔK + ΔU = 0, or K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f.  ·  **Potential energy types:** Gravitational PE near Earth: U_g = mgh (h = height above reference). Elastic PE of a spring: U_s = ½kx² (x = compression/extension from natural length). For a universal gravitational field: U = -GMm/r.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Total energy (mechanical + thermal + other) is always conserved in an isolated system.  ·  Gravitational PE: U_g = mgh (near Earth); U = −GMm/r (universal)  ·  Elastic PE: U_s = ½kx²; total spring energy: ½mv² + ½kx² = ½kA²

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Choose the reference level for PE at the lowest point to simplify calculations.  ·  The work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) and energy conservation (ΔK + ΔU = -W_nc) are DIFFERENT. The first is about NET work changing kinetic energy. The second is about total mechanical energy. With conservative forces, W_net = -ΔU, so W_net + ΔU = ΔK, which is the work-energy theorem.  ·  Inclined plane: A 3 kg block slides down a smooth 30° slope of length 10 m. Speed at bottom: v = √(2×9.8×5) = 9.9 m/s (h = 10 sin 30° = 5 m).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: In a spring-mass system, energy oscillates between kinetic and potential: ½mv² + ½kx² = constant.  ·  The work-energy theorem is more general than mechanical energy conservation — it works with friction.  ·  NEB frequently asks: 'Find the speed at the bottom' — use mgh = ½mv² for smooth surfaces.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔK) works for ALL forces — it is more general than energy conservation.  ·  The reference level for gravitational PE is arbitrary — choose it at the lowest point to simplify.  ·  In a spring-mass system, energy oscillates: ½mv² + ½kx² = ½kA² = constant.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The law of conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.  ·  The work-energy theorem states that the net work on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.  ·  Non-conservative forces (friction) convert mechanical energy into thermal energy.
